Stated Claim / Post Context:
Philadelphia police officer killed, another injured after responding to reports of man with a gun

Shane Seiber, 40, was shot and killed in west Philadelphia after responding to a report of a man with a gun, police said.

Actual Article Body:
(AP) - Philadelphia District Attorney Larry Krasner said Saturday afternoon that 35-year-old Eric Lewis is being charged with homicide for the alleged killing of a police officer early Saturday morning.

Shane Seiber, 40, was shot and killed in west Philadelphia after responding to a report of a man with a gun, police said. An officer who was with him was also shot.

Seiber, a 10-year veteran of the Philadelphia Police Department, and the other officer were transported to Penn Presbyterian Medical Center and underwent surgery, according to Police Commissioner Kevin Bethel. The surviving officer is in stable condition, Bethel said.

Along with charges for Seiber’s death, Lewis is facing a host of others, including attempted homicide, for allegedly shooting the officer and shooting at nine other officers who responded to the scene, Krasner said.

Gov. Josh Shapiro said he ordered flags to fly at half-mast for Seiber, who is survived by his wife and two children — a 7-year-old boy and a 3-year-old girl.

____

Actual Article Body:
One Philadelphia police officer is dead, and another is in stable condition after a gunman ambushed the two law enforcement officers early on Saturday morning, local officials said.

40-year-old Shane Seiber succumbed to his injuries on Saturday morning after he and his partner received a call around 1 a.m. about a man armed with a gun on the porch of a property in West Philadelphia. The two responding officers came under heavy gunfire upon approaching the home, according to Police Commissioner Kevin Bethel. Both men were immediately rushed into surgery at Penn Presbyterian Medical Center as a SWAT team and other officers arrived at the scene.

A Korean barbecue restaurant on Springvale Road was set alight just after midnight. (ABC News)

A 15-year-old boy is being treated for burns after allegedly torching a Korean barbecue restaurant in Springvale.

Police are searching for another male believed to be involved.

It is the seventh straight day of arson attacks across Melbourne.

A teenager is being treated for burns in hospital and another male is on the run after allegedly setting fire to a restaurant in Melbourne's south-east.

Just after midnight, Protectice Services Officers (PSO) patrolling Springvale Station were told that two males had broken into a Korean barbecue restaurant on Springvale Road.

Shortly after, black smoke could be seen coming from the building and firefighters were called.

Nobody was inside at the time.

The pair is believed to have fled in a vehicle before police received reports that a teenage boy with burns was at a nearby fast food restaurant on Warrigal Road in Heatherton.

The 15-year-old boy was taken to hospital under police guard and the investigation remains ongoing as officers search for the other male believed to be involved.

A jerry can was located by police near the restaurant and taken as evidence.  (ABC News)

It is the seventh straight day of arson attacks across the city.

In a botched firebombing of two vehicles in Taylors Hill, in Melbourne's north-west, on Monday morning, a 13-year-old boy suffered severe burns to 90 per cent of his body.

He remains in a critical condition and is fighting for his life.

On Friday, his sister urged other Victorian children not to accept money in exchange for carrying out crimes.

It came after it was revealed the group of youth involved in the Taylors Hill attack had been tasked with lighting the fire by middlemen on WhatsApp.
